## Context
test_cli_show_complete_or_erroring_under_write_burst costs 10.95-22.63s in recent CI samples and is the largest variable default-suite node. Closed slim-fetch-ledge is the original regression and must remain protected. Closed ambery-enigmatic-pussycat later added a generic table-driven reads-under-writer-storm property but intentionally retained the original show regression byte-for-byte. Runtime overlap alone does not prove redundancy.

## Plan
- Map both tests through the CLI, store read/reconvergence, writer process, output-completeness, exit-code, timeout, and cleanup paths.
- Enumerate the original slim-fetch-ledge failure mechanism and any failure classes only the generic property reaches.
- Seed each defect independently and run both oracles to establish a detection matrix.
- If the generic property misses any original behavior, keep both or strengthen it under legitimate RED-to-GREEN before considering consolidation.
- Measure repeated macOS and Ubuntu timings and compare concurrency-regression practice in maintained OSS projects.

## Testing / Verification
- Run `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_show_no_stall.py tests/interfaces/store/test_reads_under_sync_contention.py` with each fault seed applied independently and record the expected RED detection matrix.
- Restore production behavior and run the same focused command GREEN, including its real subprocess timeout and cleanup assertions.
- Run the repository gates with `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The original empty-or-partial-success regression remains detectable through the real CLI. (T2 unchanged; detects seeds F2/F3/F4/F6 through the real `rebar` subprocess.)
- [x] Fault-seeded evidence identifies which oracle detects every original failure class. (Matrix comment: F2/F4 both oracles; F3/F6 original only.)
- [x] Fault-seeded evidence identifies which oracle detects every generic failure class. (F5 stall and F7 `list` surface: generic only.)
- [x] Process concurrency remains real. (F1 detected only via a live lock-holder thread contending with a real CLI subprocess; 15.1s measured stall.)
- [x] Output completeness remains observable. (F3 hollow `{}`, F4 truncated, F6 missing `ticket_id` all drove RED.)
- [x] Exit status remains observable. (F2 empty-stdout-with-exit-0 drove RED in three oracles.)
- [x] Timeout enforcement remains observable. (F5: the generic 30s per-call deadline fired; the original's 60s harness default did not — band documented.)
- [x] Process cleanup remains observable. (F5: `TimeoutExpired` caught, subprocess killed, lock-holder thread joined, session ended cleanly, no orphaned processes.)
- [x] Any consolidation removes an oracle only after behavioral equivalence is proven. (Equivalence DISPROVEN; no oracle removed, no test modified.)
- [x] Repeated macOS wall-clock timings are recorded. (4 local runs 8.76/8.25/8.40/8.17s; CI macos-latest 15.34s.)
- [x] Repeated Ubuntu wall-clock timings are recorded. (3 CI job-log samples: 12.79/14.54/14.93s — sampled from run 32296354188, not executed by this session.)
- [x] Aggregate runner savings are calculated from the measured samples. (~57.6s/change across 4 pytest jobs; savings from consolidation = 0, since removal forfeits F3/F6.)
- [x] The resulting evidence cites slim-fetch-ledge and ambery-enigmatic-pussycat. (Both cited; fa6e's byte-for-byte retention confirmed correct.)
- [x] The resulting evidence cites maintained OSS concurrency-regression precedents. (Just et al. FSE 2014, Shi et al. FSE 2014, Kubernetes flaky-test policy, Go commit 011fd00, loom, PostgreSQL injection points, OpenJDK, Hypothesis; gaps flagged.)

## Outcome
**Subsumption verdict: NO.** The generic property does not subsume the original regression
(deciding seeds: F3, F6 — exit 0 with a shape-valid but content-incomplete payload). Per the
plan's stated conditional, BOTH oracles are kept. Nothing was consolidated; no test or
production file was modified.

Secondary finding (F1): reverting the actual slim-fetch-ledge fix leaves both burst tests
green — only the deterministic held-lock tests detect it. The expensive burst test does not
protect against the regression it is named for.

Follow-ups filed, both linked `discovered_from` this ticket:
- `stuckup-trophic-nabarlek` (8469-85a7) — close the generic property's proven
  partial-success gap on all four read surfaces.
- `beribboned-spherical-pipit` (ce38-2914) — right-size the storm to recover runtime
  without removing the oracle.
